name: FIRST SILICON MEASUREMENTS: die telemetry, and the board's real clock frequency
status: MEASURED (XADC telemetry, CFGMCLK frequency); one controlled re-test outstanding
why_this_iteration_exists: Every clock number in this portfolio rested on an ESTIMATED ring-oscillator frequency of ~150 MHz, and every power number was ESTIMATED. The Digilent HS2 was connected for part of this work, which made both measurable for the first time.

hardware.busdev: 1:3 (the USB bus renumbers; the SSOT's 0:4 did not answer in this session)
hardware.flash_path: openFPGALoader -c digilent_hs2 --busdev-num 1:3 <file>.bit  (SRAM load; -f means write-to-flash, not SRAM)
hardware.readback_path: tools/jtag/mpsse_jtag.py - an MPSSE transport over libftdi1, extended with a USER1 reader

measurement_1.method: openFPGALoader --read-xadc over JTAG; 5 readings 2 s apart, idle and with the design loaded
findings: Die temperature is MEASURED: 44.681 C idle, 45.271 C with the design loaded, +0.590 C. The rise is a thermal signature of the fabric doing work.
VCCINT is MEASURED at 0.99926 V, the XC7A200T -2 nominal of 1.0 V.
VCCAUX is MEASURED at 1.80532 V, the nominal of 1.8 V.
The device's own XADC min/max history reads 30.41-45.36 C and 0.9976-1.0020 V on VCCINT.
measurement_1.explicit_non_claim: This is NOT a power measurement. The XADC senses voltage and temperature, not current, and the XC7A200T has no on-die current sensor. POWER_WATTS and J/token remain ESTIMATED, and the +0.590 C rise is a thermal SIGNATURE, not a power figure.

measurement_2.method: a purpose-built probe: STARTUPE2.CFGMCLK -> an 8-bit ripple prescaler -> a 20-bit ripple binary counter -> a 32-bit BSCANE2 USER1 register read over JTAG. The counter advances once per 2^8 clock edges, so f = delta_counts * 256 / delta_seconds. Ten reads 0.5 s apart; the 20-bit counter wraps and the difference is taken modulo 2^20.
measurement_2.reference: the Artix-7 CFGMCLK family nominal is ~66 MHz (docs/fpga/clocking.md in the parent repository)
measurement_2.finding: MEASURED CFGMCLK = 67.16 MHz mean, 1.8% above the family nominal. This is a measured clock on this board, not an estimate.

measurement_3.method: the same probe with the 20-stage fabric ring oscillator in place of CFGMCLK
measurement_3.observation: the counter was FROZEN: 20 consecutive reads over a 6.7 s window all returned the identical register value 0xA5A5A5A4, with the magic intact (so the readback path works and the design is loaded). bit0 was 1 in 0/20 reads.
measurement_3.controlled_comparison: the CFGMCLK version of the SAME probe - identical counter logic, identical readback, identical register layout, only the clock source differs - returned CHANGING values on every read.
measurement_3.corroboration: the parent repository's docs/fpga/clocking.md states: 'Ring Oscillator (DOES NOT WORK) ... -abc9 inserts SCC breaker that destroys the combinational loop - Behavioral assign osc = ~osc is optimized away by Yosys - LUT1 primitive instantiation also broken by ABC9 SCC detection'.
measurement_3.status: STRONGLY SUPPORTED, one controlled re-test outstanding
measurement_3.outstanding: the frozen reading was taken with the FIRST counter implementation (a hand-rolled Gray counter whose reflected-Gray update was later found to be wrong). The controlled re-test with the IDENTICAL ripple binary counter used for the CFGMCLK measurement is built (clock_probe_ring.bit, md5 35c167a1a58015286a58b98e33fb9b9c) and was ready to flash when the Digilent HS2 dropped off the USB bus. Until that runs, the finding is reported as strongly supported rather than confirmed.

consequences_for_the_portfolio.claim_affected: the ~150 MHz ring-oscillator clock in every derived throughput figure
consequences_for_the_portfolio.status: WITHDRAWN as an estimate and now MEASURED as absent: the ring oscillator appears not to oscillate, and the board's real available clocks are CFGMCLK at 67.16 MHz measured and the 200 MHz differential oscillator on R4/T4 (not yet measured - it needs a pin-bearing design).
consequences_for_the_portfolio.action: every tok/s or J/token figure in this portfolio is re-derived against a MEASURED clock or withdrawn

consequences_for_the_portfolio.claim_affected: the shipped ternary_mac_demo_top_200t.bit and the 5.7 tok/s variance measurement
consequences_for_the_portfolio.status: SUSPECT: that bitstream clocks its counter from the SAME fabric ring oscillator, so its counter may never have advanced. The measurement's own numbers (different accumulator_final per run) need re-checking against the bitstream's actual logic.
consequences_for_the_portfolio.action: re-measure with a clocked design, or withdraw the tok/s figure

consequences_for_the_portfolio.status: still ESTIMATED, but the inputs are now real: the die runs at 45.27 C with the design loaded, VCCINT is 0.99926 V measured, and the thermal signature of the load is +0.590 C
consequences_for_the_portfolio.action: a current measurement in series with the AX7203 rail remains the only way to close it

consequences_for_the_portfolio.status: still UNKNOWN, but the question is now sharper: the design must be timed against 67.16 MHz measured (CFGMCLK) or 200 MHz (the board oscillator, unmeasured), not against an estimated 150 MHz fabric oscillator
consequences_for_the_portfolio.action: measure the R4/T4 oscillator with a pin-bearing probe

toolchain_findings: openXC7's LUT6 packing defect is bypassed by restricting the ABC mapping: `abc -lut 2` instead of the stock `abc -luts 2:2,3,6:5`. With no LUT6 in the netlist the 'No wire found for port O6' failure disappears. This is what finally made the clock probe build.

A carry-chain counter is what breaks routing in openXC7: the placer splits the CARRY4 chain across non-adjacent slices. A plain flip-flop ripple counter has no CARRY4 and routes, at the cost of a slow increment - affordable here because the counter advances once per prescaler tick.

The BSCANE2 USER1 readback works over the Digilent HS2 with a 6-bit IR (USER1 = 0x02) and this TAP framing: TLR(5) -> RTI -> Select-DR -> Select-IR -> Capture-IR -> Shift-IR -> 6 IR bits -> Update-IR -> RTI, then RTI -> Select-DR -> Capture-DR -> Shift-DR.
openFPGALoader's --read-xadc emits JSON with a trailing comma, which is not valid JSON; the fields have to be parsed with a regex.
decision: ADOPT the measured CFGMCLK (67.16 MHz) as the reference clock for any clocked design that cannot use the board's 200 MHz oscillator; withdraw every figure derived from the ~150 MHz fabric ring oscillator; record the ring-oscillator finding as strongly supported pending the controlled re-test
decision_rationale: A measured clock replaces an estimate that has now been shown to be based on a non-running clock.
The probe pair is a controlled experiment: the two designs differ in exactly one place, so the difference in behaviour localises the fault.
The honest state is written down rather than smoothed over: the confirmation run is outstanding because the cable dropped, not because the evidence is inconvenient.
still_open: The controlled re-test of the ring oscillator with the identical ripple counter (bitstream built, cable needed).
Measure the R4/T4 200 MHz differential oscillator with a pin-bearing probe - it is the clock an AX7203 design should actually use.
Re-measure or withdraw the 5.7 tok/s figure from the shipped bitstream.
POWER_WATTS and J/token: still ESTIMATED; a current measurement in series with the rail is required.
The sequential attention design still does not route in openXC7; the LUT2 mapping found here may also serve it.
method_note: Two bugs of my own were found and fixed by measurement during this iteration: the hand-rolled Gray counter (wrong update, produced a non-monotonic readback) and the host-side Gray decoder (tracked the gray bit instead of the binary bit). Both are recorded because both produced plausible-looking numbers that were wrong.
